the proposed facial recognition application based in LBP or LBP-DCT feature extraction methods with a Simplified FADAPT neural network classifier is a promising solution for face recognition applications.
the new approach based on LBP, DCT and Fuzzy ARTMAP achieves good recognition performance in two different face databases.
the proposed method achieves promising results in facial recognition, and that the fusion of Local binary patterns and discrete cosine transform provides better results than the individual features.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an incremental supervised learning method based on a Simpliﬁed Fuzzy ARTMAP neural network, for the facial recognition problem, with the purpose of improving the accuracy and the computational efﬁciency of the system.
the development of a facial recognition application based only on face detection, with the purpose of identifying the face of a person in images or video sequences.

the development of a new facial recognition application, which is based on the use of a Simplified Fuzzified Adaptive Resonance Map neural network for classification and a feature extraction method based on Local Binary Pattern or the fusion of LBP with Discrete Cosine Transform.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new approach is a good choice for face recognition.
the proposed approach achieves promising results in terms of recognition accuracy and computational efficiency.
the proposed approach is a very efficient and promising one for face recognition, which can be applied to real-time systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have presented an incremental facial recognition application, based on a supervised learning approach, with the aim of improving the accuracy of face detection and recognition.

the use of the Simplified Fuzzy ARTMAP neural network for facial recognition applications, in combination with the proposed feature extraction techniques, can provide a good alternative to existing approaches.

our approach achieves a 99.2% recognition rate on the AT&T database and a 96.4% recognition rate on Extended Yale B database, with a 0.2% false recognition rate on both databases, using a Simplified Fuzzed Adaptive Resonance Map neural network as classifier.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the new approach is capable of achieving competitive results, even with a small number of samples per subject.
the proposed approach can be used as an alternative to other facial recognition applications.
a proper feature extraction technique, together with an efficient classifier, can provide a facial recognition system with high accuracy, even for a small training set.
